Links: [{"title":"agents-sdkby Cloudflare","url":"https://mcpservers.org/agent-skills/cloudflare/agents-sdk"},{"title":"agents sdk","url":"https://skills.cat/skills/cloudflare/skills/agents-sdk"},{"title":"agents sdk","url":"https://mcpservers.org/id/agent-skills/cloudflare/agents-sdk"},{"title":"Client SDK","url":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/client-sdk"},{"title":"# MCP Transports","url":"https://unpkg.com/agents@0.24.0/docs/mcp-transports.md"},{"title":"developers.cloudflare.com","url":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/communication-channels/chat/client-sdk/index.md"},{"title":"agents sdk","url":"https://skills.sh/midudev/autoskills/agents-sdk"},{"title":"agents sdk","url":"https://llmbase.ai/skills/cloudflare/agents-sdk/"},{"title":"From cloudflare","url":"https://claudepluginhub.com/skills/kpab-cloudflare/agents-sdk"}]

The Cloudflare docs don't show a transport option on `useAgent` itself. It is a WebSocket-based React hook, and the alternative is a separate HTTP client, `agentFetch`.

- **`useAgent` is WebSocket-based.** The client SDK docs say the client SDK offers two ways to connect with a WebSocket connection, and one way to make HTTP requests. The docs list useAgent as a React hook with automatic reconnection and state management.
- **`agentFetch` is the non-WebSocket option.** It is described as the client for HTTP requests when WebSocket is not needed. The docs also say the client SDK can connect using WebSockets or HTTP.
- **Some features depend on the WebSocket.** State sync is one example: when you call `setState()`, the state is sent to the agent over WebSocket. The docs also say that when the WebSocket connection closes, the async query cache is automatically invalidated.
- **"Transport" can also mean MCP transport.** That is a separate topic. The MCP transports guide says current SDK v2 servers use createMcpHandler, a per-request stateless Worker handler with no Durable Object or WebSocket bridge. The older `McpAgent` path uses a WebSocket bridge internally.

I found no source that confirms whether `useAgent` accepts a transport setting or can fall back to HTTP. To check, look at the `useAgent` options in the Client SDK reference, or at the `agents` package source on GitHub.

input.prompt: Does useAgent support any transport other than WebSocket (e.g., HTTP, SSE, transport option)? List useAgent options related to transport/connection.

toolu_01XXw2Kt7YuFEZ3GWN4B65Wu.prompt: Does useAgent support any transport other than WebSocket (e.g., HTTP, SSE, transport option)? List useAgent options related to transport/connection.

content.content:
**No.** The page describes `useAgent` as a WebSocket client. It says the SDK offers "two ways to connect with a WebSocket connection, and one way to make HTTP requests." HTTP requests are handled by `agentFetch`, not `useAgent`. The page doesn't mention SSE or a transport option.

**Connection-related `useAgent` options:**

- `host`: custom host (defaults to the current origin)
- `path`: custom path prefix
- `name`: instance name (defaults to `"default"`)
- `query`: query parameters sent on connection, either a static object or an async function
- `queryDeps`: dependencies that trigger re-running an async `query`
- `cacheTtl`: cache TTL for the query result (default: 5 minutes)
- `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onError`, `onMessage`: connection event handlers

**Related return members:** `send(data)` sends a raw WebSocket message, `close()` closes the connection, and `reconnect()` forces a reconnection.

content.text:
I'm assuming you mean `useAgent` from Cloudflare's Agents SDK (`agents/react`). If so, the answer is none: it only connects over WebSockets. Its connection options (`host`, `path`, `name`, `query`, `cacheTtl`, `onOpen`/`onClose`/`onError`/`onMessage`) are all for WebSockets, and the docs don't mention any transport setting, HTTP fallback or SSE. When you don't need a WebSocket, the SDK gives you a separate function, `agentFetch`, for plain HTTP requests to the agent. You lose some features that way, such as automatic state sync through `setState()`, which runs over the WebSocket. MCP servers have their own transport options, but those are a separate topic and don't change how `useAgent` connects.

If you meant a `useAgent` from another library, tell me which one and I'll look it up.

Sources:
- [Client SDK – Cloudflare Agents docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/client-sdk)
- [Chat client SDK – Cloudflare docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/communication-channels/chat/client-sdk/index.md)
- [MCP Transports (agents@0.24.0)](https://unpkg.com/agents@0.24.0/docs/mcp-transports.md)
